samples.summary: Splitting a bulleted heading drops the remembered `headingLevel`, so only the FIRST bullet honours the new heading-restoring Enter/Backspace exit
samples.evidence: The delta makes `splitBlock`/`deleteBackward` exit an empty list-item via `unlistedBlockType(block)` (document.ts:304, :267) with the comment "so Enter matches Backspace and the toggle". But the non-empty split path chooses `newType = 'list-item'` (document.ts:330-331) and `applySplitBlock` then does `if (newBlockType !== 'heading') delete after.headingLevel` (block-helpers.ts:256-258); the Yorkie store does the same (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049 only copies headingLevel when `newBlockType === 'heading'`). Real flow: bullet a Heading 2, type text, press Enter → the new bullet has no `headingLevel`; press Enter again on that empty bullet → it exits to a *paragraph*, while the original bullet would have exited to Heading 2. The stated invariant ("a `list-item` retains the level of the heading it was made from", docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-128) is violated by the split, so the new exit is inconsistent from the second line onward.

samples.summary: Word/line Backspace bypasses the empty-list-item exit branch on the first block
samples.evidence: `handleWordBackspace` returns early when `this.doc.getBlockIndex(pos.blockId) === 0` (text-editor.ts:2003) and `handleLineBackspace` does the same (text-editor.ts:2805) *before* calling `doc.deleteBackward`. The branch the delta modifies in `deleteBackward` (document.ts:264-270) deliberately sits before the `blockIndex <= 0` guard so it fires for the first block, but these two callers never reach it: Cmd/Alt+Backspace on an empty bulleted heading that is the first block does nothing, while plain Backspace now converts it back to a heading. Inconsistent list-exit behaviour across the three Backspace entry points.

samples.summary: A bulleted `title`/`subtitle` still exits to a paragraph, silently downgrading the block
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:337-344) only remembers `headingLevel`; `MemDocStore.setBlockType` (memory.ts:250-263) drops the original `type` when converting to `list-item`, and `title`/`subtitle` carry no level. So Backspace/Enter on an empty bulleted Title returns a `paragraph`, losing the Title style, whereas a bulleted Heading is restored. Same asymmetry as the toolbar toggle, but the delta's comments claim exit parity.

But the non-empty split path chooses `newType = 'list-item'` (document.ts:330-331) and `applySplitBlock` then does `if (newBlockType !== 'heading') delete after.headingLevel` (block-helpers.ts:256-258); the Yorkie store does the same (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049 only copies headingLevel when `newBlockType === 'heading'`). verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `unlistedBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:337-344) restores a heading only when `block.headingLevel !== undefined`, and both new keyboard exits depend on it (document.ts:303-306 Enter, document.ts:264-269 Backspace). But the non-empty split path picks `newType = 'list-item'` (document.ts:329-331) and `applySplitBlock` deletes the remembered level for any non-heading target while explicitly preserving listKind/listLevel (block-helpers.ts:254-263); MemDocStore routes through it (memory.ts:226-231) and the Yorkie store copies `headingLevel` only when `newBlockType === 'heading'` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049-2051, 2139-2141) and reuses `applySplitBlock` for its cache (2147). Meanwhile `setBlockType` in both stores deliberately keeps the level when converting to a list-item (memory.ts:258-260; yorkie-doc-store.ts:1391-1395,1458), and docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134 documents that a list-item retains the level and that every list-exit path goes through `unlistedBlockType`. No compensating restore exists in the view layer (text-editor.ts:362-368, 2036-2092 simply forward to doc.splitBlock). Result: after splitting a bulleted heading, the new bullet has no headingLevel, so its Enter/Backspace exit yields a paragraph while the original yields Heading 2 — an inconsistent, invariant-violating state, and clearly wrong for a mid-text split where a plain heading would keep its type (document.ts:332-337). Nothing here supports not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.
